_comment: World frame for the whole game. NEVER change origin after meshes are imported: every region is generated into this single frame so expansion is just adding a region.

frame.horizontal: local ENU tangent plane at origin (WGS84), matches CesiumGeoreference
frame.vertical: NAVD88 orthometric height in meters (curvature ignored; <0.4 m drop at 2 km)
frame.ue_axes: UE X = East, UE Y = South (-North), UE Z = Up, centimeters (same as Cesium for Unreal)

source_units._comment: Cambridge GIS elevations/heights are US survey feet (verified: MIT Bldg 54 TOP_GL = 327.4).

mit_core._comment: Stage B (2026-10-05): Harvard + MIT = the City of Cambridge between the Charles and the Somerville line (wall 100 m inside it), from just west of Harvard Sq / the Common / the Radcliffe Quad to Kendall. Stage A was bbox [-71.1085, 42.354, -71.08, 42.37]. Region id kept as mit_core. See wip_notes2/STAGE_B_PLAN.md

playable._comment: region = bbox ∩ city.buffer(city_buffer_m) − (city land boundary, not in the river).buffer(land_boundary_inset_m); the part containing the spawn (geo.region_polygon)

spawn._comment: Mass Ave northbound, just north of Memorial Dr (77 Mass Ave side)

buildings._comment: build_meshes.py rules; regions without this block keep the Stage A behaviour

_tiles_comment: Defaults for regions without their own camb3d_tiles / boston_tiles (geo.region_cfg)

boston._comment: City of Boston Planning Department 3D Smart Model (PDDL per Analyze Boston; credit the City). Same MA State Plane grid and offset as the Cambridge tiles.
